headline: A former Google DeepMind researcher who worked on AlphaGo argues that today's chatbots do not truly reason and that making them bigger will not fix that.
score_reason: A named expert's opinion essay published today, with no new research results.
importance_line: Researchers and companies building AI for science, medicine and engineering are the audience, since the author says trust there needs reasoning that can be checked, but this is one expert's opinion and the essay gives no new test results.
summary: In an opinion essay for MIT Technology Review, Thore Graepel, chair of machine learning at University College London who worked on AlphaGo at DeepMind, argues that chatbots only predict the next word, even when they write out step-by-step thinking, so they lack the open record of what they believe and doubt that scientific reasoning needs. He says this is why he recently left Google DeepMind, and he calls for systems that keep such a record and check each step against evidence, as AlphaGo did when it searched moves ahead.
notes: Opinion essay, not a news report or research result; written in the author's voice.
